Definition: from G5346; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"):--fame.
BiblicalUsage: Pheme is a saying, a rumour, a fame, and it spreads faster than any messenger. Jesus returns in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and His fame goes out through all the region round about, and the fame of the raising of the ruler's daughter spreads abroad into all that land.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fame in the gospels is the sound of works that cannot be hidden: the word of Jesus' deeds ran ahead of Him into every town.
